question: ow ow ow touched the camp stove grate with my fingers
keyPoints: Cool the burn with cool water (not ice)
Cover it with a clean dressing; don't put butter or ointments on it

question: my buddy's sleeve caught on the fire for a sec, his forearm is all white and leathery now
keyPoints: This is a deep burn: cool only briefly, cover with cool moist clean dressing, don't pull off stuck clothing
Needs medical care right away
redFlags: Soak a deep burn in cold water

question: theres so much blood coming out of his thigh it wont stop
keyPoints: Press hard directly on the bleeding
If pressure doesn't stop it on a limb, tourniquet 2-3 inches above the wound; get help

question: the gauze i put on is totally red now, do i peel it off?
keyPoints: Don't remove it; add more on top and keep pressing
If it keeps soaking through on a limb, use a tourniquet

question: stepped wrong off a log and now my ankle is fat and purple
keyPoints: Rest, cold, compression, elevation
Could be a break if it can't bear weight or there was a pop; splint and get it checked

question: pretty sure her wrist is broken, it's bent the wrong way
keyPoints: Splint it as found so the joints above and below can't move
Check circulation below before and after; remove rings/watches

question: he bonked his head on a branch and now he's kinda out of it and throwing up
keyPoints: Signs of a concussion or worse: watch closely, keep still if the neck may be hurt
Get medical help

question: she's grabbing her throat and can't make a sound!!
keyPoints: Five back blows then abdominal thrusts until it comes out
If she passes out, start CPR

question: he's not moving and I can't tell if he's breathing at all
keyPoints: Check breathing and open the airway
If not breathing, call for help and start CPR (hard fast chest pushes)

question: my friend won't stop shivering and she's slurring her words
keyPoints: Signs of hypothermia: get her out of wind and wet, dry clothes
Insulate under and over, warm sweet drinks if awake, handle gently, get help

question: can't feel my fingertips and they've gone kind of waxy
keyPoints: Possible frostbite: rewarm in warm (not hot) water
Don't rub it, don't hold it near a fire

question: feel super dizzy and sweaty and kinda sick after hiking in the sun
keyPoints: Heat exhaustion: shade, lie down, cool wet cloths, sip water
Get help if not better in 30 minutes; hot dry skin or confusion is heat stroke

question: something stung my leg and theres a little black thing stuck in it
keyPoints: Scrape the stinger out sideways; don't squeeze it
Wash, cold compress; watch for trouble breathing or swelling

question: a snake just got my ankle, two little holes
keyPoints: Keep still and calm, remove tight items, get to medical care fast
Don't cut, suck, tourniquet or ice

question: there's a tick dug into my armpit ew
keyPoints: Grip it close to the skin with fine tweezers and pull straight out slowly
Wash, watch for rash or fever over the next weeks; don't twist or squeeze

question: brushed through some leafy stuff and now my legs are itchy and bumpy
keyPoints: Could be a plant rash like poison ivy: wash with soap and cold water
Don't scratch; clean gear that touched it

question: his lips are swelling up and he's wheezing after eating trail mix
keyPoints: Severe allergic reaction: emergency, get help now
Use his epinephrine auto-injector if he has one

question: is the creek water ok to just drink
keyPoints: Treat it first
Boil (1 minute, 3 at altitude) or use tablets/iodine/bleach

question: how do i get a fire going, i've only got a lighter and some sticks
keyPoints: Gather tinder, kindling and bigger wood first
Light the tinder from the bottom, add kindling gradually with air gaps

question: i have literally no idea where the trail went
keyPoints: Stop and take stock before deciding
Staying put is often better; move only if sure it gets you to water, shelter, help

question: sun's going down and we're stuck out here, what do we sleep under
keyPoints: Pick a safe spot (not flood/rockfall/dead trees) and use natural cover or a tarp
Insulate from the ground; block the wind

question: freezing in my tent, sleeping bag is thin
keyPoints: Insulate from the ground, stay dry, block wind
Loose layers, cover head; don't use a stove in a closed tent
redFlags: Use a stove/candle in a closed tent

question: haven't peed all day and my head is pounding
keyPoints: Likely dehydration: rest in shade and drink water in small sips
Get help if confused or not improving

question: got some grit in my eye and it wont stop watering
keyPoints: Flush with clean water
Don't rub; if something is stuck or it's cut, cover loosely and get help

question: my friend just collapsed and is jerking all over
keyPoints: Protect them from hitting things; don't hold them down or put anything in the mouth
Afterwards put them on their side; get help if it lasts over 5 minutes or repeats

question: my diabetic buddy is all shaky and sweaty and not making sense
keyPoints: Suspect low blood sugar: if they can swallow, give sugar
Nothing by mouth if they can't swallow; get help if no quick improvement

question: way up on the mountain and my head is killing me and i feel like puking
keyPoints: Could be altitude illness
Don't go higher; go down if it gets worse or with confusion or breathlessness

question: sliced my thumb whittling a stick
keyPoints: Press on it to stop the bleeding
Rinse well with clean water, cover it, check daily for infection

question: my feet have been soaking wet in my boots for two days and they're numb and wrinkly
keyPoints: Immersion (trench) foot: dry and warm them gently
Don't rub; clean dry socks, raise them, get it checked if it worsens

question: these red berries look tasty, can i eat em
keyPoints: Only if positively identified; don't go by looks
If unsure, don't eat them
